bug_semantics: Authenticated IDOR on POST /xxl-job-admin/jobinfo/remove: JobInfoController.remove() takes a client-supplied numeric job ID and calls XxlJobService.remove(id), which loads that row and deletes the job plus its logs/GLUE with no job-group authorization. PermissionInterceptor requires login by default but not admin. After executor-dimension ACLs exist, a logged-in non-admin whose permission string is empty (or omits the target group) cannot see foreign jobs in the UI yet can enumerate IDs and delete them. add/update later called validJobGroupPermission on jobGroup; remove/stop/start did not until 3.2.0. CWE-639 / CWE-99.
flaw_origin: d66bdc88113ed9e25b09b6a3b547338e794b0f0a (2017-03-12) first wrote JobInfoController.remove(int id) { return xxlJobService.remove(id); } and the matching service delete-by-id, replacing parent f3573c86's remove(int jobGroup, String jobName). Those ID-only lines never checked object-level permission. 7ccdd75d (2019-05-04) added executor-dimension ACLs but only filtered the job-list UI, so the pre-existing ID delete became a cross-group IDOR. git blame at 3.1.1 points at 6fd7c943 (equal-ins/del whitespace rewrite) and d3a88e41 only added @RequestParam; neither is a first-write. a09f7f30 later added validJobGroupPermission to add/update and still left remove unchecked.
